subject.title: [Feature]: Add per-channel identity override for Discord bindings

question: Should ordinary Discord routed replies support per-binding or per-agent visible identity, and should the approved mechanism be webhook persona delivery, bot self-profile mutation, a binding nickname field, or deferral?
rationale: The requested behavior would create a new public config/action surface around bot-token-backed visible identity, so automation should not choose the product model, credential boundary, fallback semantics, or security gate without maintainer intent.

options.title: Approve webhook persona delivery
options.body: Add a Discord plugin-owned routed-reply identity path that reuses webhook username/avatar delivery with explicit credential handling, fallback behavior, docs, tests, and live Discord proof.

options.title: Coordinate with self-profile work
options.body: Treat this as part of the Discord self-profile decision and only add nickname or avatar mutation if maintainers accept the cross-channel identity semantics and security boundary.

options.title: Defer per-binding identity
options.body: Keep current bot-account replies plus thread-bound webhook persona behavior and ask users to use multiple bot accounts or existing thread-bound flows for now.

recommendation.title: Approve webhook persona delivery
recommendation.body: Add a Discord plugin-owned routed-reply identity path that reuses webhook username/avatar delivery with explicit credential handling, fallback behavior, docs, tests, and live Discord proof.

likelyOwner.reason: They own the closest merged Discord webhook/persona delivery path and can judge whether that primitive should extend to ordinary routed replies.
